To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the global mean CALIPO AOT is improved by 0.01 by replacing RFV extinction values with a derived noise floor, and that the occurrence frequency of all-RFV aerosol extinction profiles is nearly 50% for cloud-free daytime CALIOP aerosol data.
the global mean AOT for CALIOP L1 532 nm profiles is 0.15, and that CALIOP AOD retrievals for profiles containing all-RFV values should be replaced by a noise-floor value of 0.08.
CALIOP LIDAR data products contain many profiles with no detectable aerosol, and that these profiles have a significant impact on global aerosol retrievals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of CALIOP all RFV profiles on aerosol optical properties and their subsequent impact on the CALIOP AOD retrieval.
the impact of RFV values in CALIOP L1 data products on the accuracy of the derived L2 AOT, as well as the impact of the derived noise floor on the accuracy of CALIOP-based climatologies of AOT.
identifying and quantifying biases in CALIOP L3 AOT climatological data due to the presence of all-RFV aerosol profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the CALIPSO L2 AOT data for climatological purposes is not appropriate without the correction for the RFVs, and the proposed method for the RFVs correction should be applied.

the current practice of reporting zero AOT for all all-RFV aerosol profiles in the L2 CALIOP aerosol data products is not appropriate and that a more realistic approach is to use an estimate of the mean extinction for all-RFVs, as described herein.

the use of a noise floor to replace the RFV values in all-RFV CALIOP profiles is recommended for improving CALIOP-derived AOT climatological products, and that such an approach may be applied to other L2 products that contain RFV values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CALIOP all-daytime RFV profiles are not truly "aerosol-free" and that their AOT values are underestimated by a factor of about two.
the CALIOP AOD is likely underestimated for all-RFVs profiles.

the CALIOP all-daytime aerosol extinction profiles with RFVs are likely not truly devoid of aerosol, but rather represent a detection sensitivity threshold below which aerosol cannot be detected by the lidar.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CALIOP L1 and L2 products should be revised to report the AOT of all-RFV CALIOP profiles as being non-zero, with the revised values being based on the derived noise floor and the MODIS DT (and AERONET) collocations.
, when using CALIOP L3 AOT climatological products, it is important to be cognizant of the potential for bias introduced by the use of RFV values in the L2 extinction profiles.

the CALIOP L1 and L2 data products do not adequately represent the presence of aerosol in all-RFV aerosol extinction profiles, and that this omission can lead to an underestimate in the CALIOP AOD climatology.
